description:
MSRV is already 1.88 (workspace Cargo.toml:46), but let-chains in if/while conditions are gated behind Rust edition 2024, not the toolchain version. The workspace is currently on edition 2021 (Cargo.toml:39).

Discovered via bd:JMAP-26di.54 attempt: 12 sites in jmap-chat-client/src/methods/space.rs refactored to 'if let Some(x) = expr && !x.is_empty() { ... }' produced 'error: let chains are only allowed in Rust 2024 or later'. Confirmed by subagent compile check.

The edition bump is a workspace-architectural decision affecting all 30 crates. Considerations:
- All crates inherit via 'edition.workspace = true' so the change is a single line in workspace Cargo.toml.
- Edition 2024 changes some name resolution, lifetime defaults (Rust 2024 lifetime capture rules), and pattern matching semantics. Most code is unaffected but the migration may require small fixes.
- 'cargo fix --edition' can mechanically handle most migration churn.
- After the bump, the bd:JMAP-26di.54 refactor can be applied immediately, and similar nested-if patterns workspace-wide can be cleaned up.

Acceptance criteria:
1. cargo fix --edition --allow-dirty --workspace runs to completion.
2. cargo test --workspace passes.
3. cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings clean.
4. Cargo.toml workspace.package edition = '2024'.
5. After the bump, re-open bd:JMAP-26di.54 and apply the let-chain refactor.

Scope: workspace-wide, but the migration tool (cargo fix --edition) handles most of it mechanically. Estimate: 1-2 hour task including any manual cleanup.

Cross-references:
- bd:JMAP-26di.54 (blocked on this)
- Workspace AGENTS.md 'Build & Test' commands stay the same — no agent-facing churn.
title: Workspace edition bump to 2024 to unlock let-chains and 2024-edition idioms
